I believe the we can't be certain of anything. That we have to take natural assumptions like "This world is real. I'm real. ..." etc before we can deal with evidence at all.

My issue is that there's a lot of those assumptions. Not just about everything (i.e. the world/I'm real) but also specifics (i.e. the laws of our universe do not change therefore <stuff based on evidence we've collected based on that presupposition is true>).

My issue with the specific example I gave is that you can't test that into the past, because it relies on itself to do the testing. Meaning, saying "we know they haven't because: <evidence of things we've measured from the past>" is circular reasoning, the same way "The Bible is right because God says it is" is.

The problem is, if you can't blindly take that on faith (which you'd have to, imo), you can't be certain about anything (i.e. what I said to begin with what I believe).

The best thing I think we can have is written history because a change in physics would be something humanity would notate. The issue is that written history is like 7,000ish years while the universe is supposedly 13.7 Billion years old (I say supposedly because that claim is based on evidence garnered using the laws of physics and presupposing they are constant and always have been and always will be).

7,000 years to judge 13.7 Billion years is like doing an experiment for a year, taking the last 16.11 (I did the math) seconds and using that to say that's how it's been for the entire year. If it's the best you've got, then ok, but any scientist who did that would be a laughing stock if he wanted his results to be taken seriously.

You get the idea. You can't say "The laws of physics have been constant." because any evidence used to prove that claim would require using the laws of physics over time. Which is inherently circular logic. You could say that "That's not the claim. The claim is that they have changed." but I think they are the same thing so it doesn't matter. It's not the same (imo) as the "God is real" vs "God isn't real" thing.

Constance vs change isn't the same thing imo as Real vs Not Real. I guess you could change the way the question is asked to make it more similar, but I think getting into semantics only serves the purpose of trying to not ask a question that someone is uncomfortable asking.

Anyway, you get the idea. It's the best we've got. I just keep in mind that nothing is certain. Layer on top that science changes all the time as new evidence of things is found and I just don't worry about claims being made anymore.

Unfortunately, a side effect of this view on life is that Science doesn't really excite me anymore unless it has something I can tangibly touch and show that it works and is cool. i.e. "moving 13 Terabytes/s in a lab with the cool new technique" means nothing to me until I am doing it in my home/office. Or "<percentage> of the universe is made up of <element>" means nothing to me beyond "cool thing to know, even if it's almost certainly wrong". But most fun facts are anyway, so mixed bag n all that.

You get the idea. I'll stop now.
